title: How to Edit Demo Data With AI: Tips and Top Software
summary: Real, relevant data assures potential customers that your product is really built for them. Here are 4 tips to edit your data quicker with AI.
body_markdown:
The more your demo looks and feels like your product, the better it will land with potential customers.


Some of that comes from your product’s UI and UX, but a lot comes from the data you present.


Real, relevant data assures potential customers that yes, your product really *does* work the way they expect it to, and is built *specifically* to support the kinds of tasks they do on a daily basis.


The problem is, most demo environments are empty or messy. Which means someone spends time populating or cleaning them up before every live demo.


According to our 2026 State of Demo Automation Data report,[41% of SEs](https://www.navattic.com/report/state-of-demo-automation-2026) manually update their demo environment.


For a few one-off demos, taking the time to personalize by hand might be worth it. But manually customizing every demo eats up time that reps and SEs could spend talking to leads.


Below, we share four ways to expedite the editing process with AI, plus the tools to do it.


4 Tips to Edit Your Demo Data with AI


### 1. Personalize Existing Demos For Specific Prospects


Instead of spinning up new sandboxes from scratch, clone existing[interactive demos](https://www.navattic.com/blog/interactive-demos) and overlay personalized data.


For example, if you already have a generic “feature xyz” or “vertical abc” kind of demo, make a copy and then insert[personalization variables](https://docs.navattic.com/demos/personalized#personalize-your-captures) like:


- First name
- Role
- Company name
- Company logo


While these may feel like very small touches (that really only take a few clicks), people really notice. Per[Alexander Yant at Slope](https://www.navattic.com/blog/customer-interview-series-personalized-demo-environments-with-alexander-yant) :


*“Prospects really enjoy the personalized aspects of our demos. It can help relax any tensions and make it seem less like a rigid sales experience and more of a fun conversation.”*


Showing you know who you’re talking to and choosing a specific demo makes prospects feel special and connected to your product.


At the very least, it gets them engaged enough to click through – which may lead them straight to an aha moment they didn’t expect.


In fact, one of our customers, PowerSchool, found that[over 90% of their deals](http://navattic.com/customers/powerschool) start from an interactive demo.


### 2. Update UI Without Rebuilding the Whole Demo


Unlike a product video where you have to refilm everything to make even the smallest of customer callouts,[interactive demo software](https://www.navattic.com/blog/what-is-demo-software) makes it easy to update elements like, say, your navbar, across every screen at once.


It's why[Traackr](https://www.navattic.com/customers/traackr) , a system of record for data-driven influencer marketing, uses interactive demos over videos:


*“Overall, it's a better experience for us and our audience compared to video content. Interactive demos are easier to create, update, and click through for end users.”*


In Navattic, for instance, you can use the[Capture Editor or prompt Copilot](https://www.navattic.com/blog/four-ways-to-use-navattic-s-capture-editor) , our AI assistant, to make the changes you want across every flow in seconds.


This is particularly useful for SEs and reps trying to make prospects aware of all the new AI features their company is putting out.


As[Shawn Xiaoyang Hu](https://www.linkedin.com/in/shawn-xiaoyang-hu-75ba6a35/) at Cisco[points out](https://www.g2.com/products/navattic/reviews/navattic-review-11431266) , *“Continuous application updates cause challenges in content management. Navattic demo flows always deliver consistent experiences to our demo users because when the app is updated, we can easily update all of our demos.”*


### 3. Update a Table or Chart in a Few Steps


Finding or building the right dataset to upload (and making sure it doesn’t violate privacy regulations) has always been time-consuming.


But now, the best interactive demo tools let you create “up and to the right”-looking charts and industry-specific data by describing them to an AI assistant in plain English.


Navattic’s AI Copilot has[helped one Navattic user](https://www.g2.com/products/navattic/reviews/navattic-review-12656707) cut down the time it takes to *“Go from ‘We need a demo for this use case’ to something ready to share.”*


### 4. Remove or Blur Unnecessary Information


Oftentimes, there are parts of your product that aren’t quite ready for public consumption.


Normally, you’d either have to:


1. Get strategic with your cropping or editing to make sure those parts don’t get exposed in a screenshot or product video.
2. Request a special demo environment without those elements, which could take weeks to turn around.


With an AI-driven interactive demo platform, you can prompt an assistant to do things like:


- Blur sensitive data
- Find and replace certain phrases or numbers (or delete them)
- Remove irrelevant UI
- Make other final touches to your captures


All without the help of your product or engineering team.


[The team at Insider](http://navattic.com/customer/highlights/insider) highlights: *“We did not need to involve a single engineering resource to design, build, or launch the interactive demo experiences.”*


Data Injection vs Cloning: Pros and Cons


While most[demo software](https://www.navattic.com/blog/what-is-demo-software#Testbox) companies have built-in editing functionality these days, they differ in their implementation.


Either they inject new data into your product environment, or they make a copy of your product environment and then edit it.


There are advantages and disadvantages to each approach:


### Data Injection


**Best fit for:** Teams that cater to buyers in highly regulated or technical industries who usually require a full-blown POC – and have the resources to absorb setup time and cost.


Tools like Saleo, Testbox, and Reprise dynamically change the underlying data in your product. As you might guess, this is a big (and expensive) feat.


Testbox starts at $44,750 per year. Reprise and Saleo don’t publicly share pricing, but Vendr’s median price for Reprise is $31,600 per year, and for Saleo it’s $54,000 per year.


All three are significantly more expensive than most demo software.


#### When Data Injection is Worth the Price:


- **You need real data.** If a prospect will not sign on the dotted line without seeing how your product behaves with their specific data, injection is the way to go. *“I like how intuitive the platform is for tailoring demos to different audiences, ensuring a polished, real-time experience for prospects. The ability to showcase the product in a controlled yet realistic way has significantly improved our sales and customer engagement.”* ([Reprise G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/reprise-demos/reviews/reprise-review-11609206) )
- **You want to show a full-on demo environment.** Sometimes customers (read: procurement or IT teams) are very discerning and want to get a true POC. In these cases, a full sandbox with real demo data may be a must-have to close the deal. *“Being able to walk customers through a live, hands-on version of the product allows them to see how \[the product\] works in real scenarios, rather than just hearing about its features in theory. They can explore the interface, test workflows, and get a true sense of how the platform will support their day-to-day business operations.”* ([Testbox G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/testbox/reviews/testbox-review-11658770) )


#### You Might Still Deal With:


- **Drag.** Adding real data to the backend of your product can slow your environment down. Users say things like *“At peak times, when several users are logged in at once, we have noticed the system can slow down a bit,”* ([Testbox G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/testbox/reviews/testbox-review-11665044) ) and *“It does take a while to load. If \[there is\] unstable internet connection \[at\] conferences, it does slow it down.”* ([Reprise G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/reprise-demos/reviews/reprise-review-11719649) )
- **Bugs.** ** Because you’re editing your real product environment, your demo will inherit any undetected issues. Per real users: *“Occasionally, the environment can be unstable, with crashes or unexpected bugs disrupting the flow of a demonstration. These issues, while infrequent, can be distracting and may cause clients to lose focus on the product’s real strengths,”* and ([Testbox G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/testbox/reviews/testbox-review-11658770) ) *“Saleo occasionally experiences bugs that, despite being fixed quickly, can sometimes disrupt usage. The main issue is that these bugs often become apparent during live presentations, which can make it challenging to rely on the tool with full confidence.”* ([Saleo G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/saleo/reviews/saleo-review-10932746) )
- **Maintenance.** Updating every sandbox with real data takes effort. Users say things like, *“Extremely manual to set up. It is rigid. If you have feature updates that you want to pull into your demo environment, you basically have to build it again from scratch, and it's not easy to do,”* ([Reprise G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/reprise-demos/reviews/reprise-review-7793437) ) and *“Certain advanced customization features demand highly specific instructions tailored to the particular site, which can make the initial setup process time-consuming. Furthermore, making adjustments to a tour after it has been captured can sometimes be challenging.”* ([Saleo G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/saleo/reviews/saleo-review-12106289) )


### Cloning


**Best fit for:** Teams prioritizing speed and shareability over full-product coverage.


Cloning lets you personalize your demos at scale, making it much easier for anyone on the GTM team to use and repurpose demos at any point in the sales cycle.


Navattic, Walnut, and Storylane all make an HTML/CSS copy of your product that you can then edit however you want.


They’re not as pricey as the Testbox, Reprise, and Saleos of the world, and they don’t take as long to set up, which means you can use them across the full sales cycle (not just for a live demo).


#### What Cloning Offers:


- **Editing via an AI prompt.**[Navattic’s Copilot](https://www.navattic.com/product/copilot) lets you change virtually anything about your demo (personalization variables, branding, cropping, adjusting tables and charts) with a simple prompt – in one capture or across your whole flow. *“There isn’t much of a learning curve, and Copilot helps you spin new demos up quickly.”* ([Navattic G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/navattic/reviews/navattic-review-12439295) )
- **Assets you can share across the sales cycle.** Because your demo is a lightweight copy of your product, you can use it anywhere in the funnel: pre-call emails, demo follow-ups, even for partner training or customer onboarding. *“It simplifies client follow-ups and helps engage prospects early by showcasing key workflows, making the process efficient and impactful.”* ([Navattic G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/navattic/reviews/navattic-review-13505597) ) *“Storylane allows us to simulate a live walkthrough and embed it in our learning management system. This is so valuable to our customer experience and managing the time of our trainers. Customers and click through and follow along as if we were training them live.”* ([Storylane G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/storylane/reviews/storylane-review-13484463) )
- **Full control over what you show.** You don’t have to gloss over any half-finished features, you can simply remove them. Users say, *“Navattic gives us the flexibility to highlight specific Sage Intacct use cases without needing to build or deliver a full demo every time. I particularly value the capture and editing tools, tooltips, beacons, and branching flows that help build polished, interactive demos focusing on the right features,”* ([Navattic G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/navattic/reviews/navattic-review-13472632) ) and *“My greatest benefit in Walnut is that I will be able to influence the story of each demo. I used to rely on our production environment before Walnut, which occasionally revealed rough edges.”* ([Walnut G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/walnut/reviews/walnut-review-12329139) )


#### You Might Still Deal With:


- **Skepticism.** If your demo spans multiple workflows or modules, it can be a little harder to show the breadth of your product in a copied environment. *“There’s definitely a limit to how much you can realistically show in a click-through demo. Once you get into more complicated configurations, custom logic, or workflows that depend on a lot of different variables, it’s hard to make the experience feel truly representative. Those kinds of scenarios are still better handled in a live session.”* ([Storylane G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/storylane/reviews/storylane-review-13477764) )


That said, some interactive demo tools like Navattic let you[create sandbox demos](https://docs.navattic.com/launchpad/demos/sandbox#building-a-sandbox-demo) if you need to show off your entire product.


### It’s Not Either/Or


One final note here: you don’t have to stick to one or the other. Some teams use injection for live demos and POCs and cloning to share that demo throughout the sales cycle.
